name: Israel Englander
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Israel Englander founded Millennium Management in 1989 with $35 million. Now, the hedge fund firm manages over $92 billion.
Israel Englander, or Izzy, is the son of Polish immigrants.
Englander's hedge fund uses a multi-manager platform, feeding more capital to those who perform well and getting rid of traders who perform poorly.
Englander once backed a professional gambler named Jeff Yass, who began trading on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange in 1981 and  has since become a billionaire.

name: Yu Yong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)
forbes_bio: Yu Yong's wealth mainly comes from his holdings in CMOC Group, formerly China Molybdenum, one of the world's largest producers of the metal.
He also owns a stake in global lithium-ion battery leader CATL.
Yu's investment holding firm Cathay Fortune is an early investor in Zeekr, an electric vehicle brand under China's automobile giant Geely. Zeekr went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2024.
In June 2025, CMOC took Canada-listed Lumina Gold private in a $419 million deal. Lumina fully owns the Cangrejos gold-copper project in Ecuador.

name: Hamdi Ulukaya
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: Hamdi Ulukaya, known as the yogurt king, is the founder of America's most popular Greek yogurt brand, Chobani.
Ulukaya grew up in a Kurdish dairy-farming family in Turkey and raised sheep. He eventually left to study political science at Ankara University.
He immigrated to the U.S. in 1994 to study English in upstate New York, an area that reminded him of the small farming villages in Eastern Turkey.
With a loan from the Small Business Administration, he bought an old yogurt plant there in 2005 and developed a recipe inspired by his heritage.
He started selling his yogurt in 2007; in 2023, Chobani pulled in more than $2 billion in sales.
forbes_facts: In January 2018, Ulukaya married Louise Vongerichten, daughter of world-renowned French chef Jean Georges Vongerichten. The couple welcomed a son later that year.
Refugees and immigrants, who make up 30% Chobani's workforce, are offered English language classes as well as translators in up to 11 languages.

name: Andre Esteves
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Andre Esteves is chairman of Brazilian investment bank, BTG Pactual.
Esteves, who started with BTG as an intern, sold the company to Swiss banking giant UBS in 2006 for $3.1 billion, forming the Brazilian subsidiary UBS Pactual.
In 2009 he engineered the sale of UBS Pactual to investment firm BTG and became chairman of the board and CEO of the new firm.
He was accused of obstruction of justice for Brazil's largest corruption scandal, Operation Car Wash, and jailed for almost three weeks in 2015. He was acquitted in 2018 and returned to BTG.
BTG Pactual announced plans in 2025 to buyout minority shareholders of Banco Pan at a premium in a bid to make the publicly-traded Brazilian bank a wholly-owned subsidiary.
forbes_facts: After he was detained in 2015, Esteves stepped down as CEO and gave up his seat on BTG's board.

name: Yang Shaopeng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026)
forbes_bio: Yang Shaopeng's fortune derives from a stake in SITC International Holdings, a shipping and logistics company.
Yang stepped down as chairman in 2024; then CEO Yang Xianxiang, not related to him, took over the position.
Yang Shaopeng's daughter Yang Xin is the company's vice chairman.

name: Matthias Reimann-Andersen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Matthias Reimann-Andersen and three of his siblings own 95% of Luxembourg-based investment firm JAB Holding Company s.? r.l (JAB).
Upon the death of their father in 1984, Matthias and eight other heirs each inherited 11.1% of JAB; five of them subsequently divested their stakes.
The brands associated with the Reimann fortune include Pret A Manger, Krispy Kreme donuts, Peet's Coffee and Panera Bread.
Matthias is a descendant of chemist Ludwig Reimann, who, in 1828, joined with Johann Adam Benckiser and his namesake chemical company.
JAB made its first foray into the pet care sector in 2019 with the acquisition of Compassion-First Pet Hospitals.
forbes_facts: In 2016, the Reimanns commissioned a study which revealed close ties between their family, its business and the Nazi regime during World War II.
Following this discovery, the family formed the Alfred Landecker Foundation to support Holocaust survivors, conduct research and combat antisemitism.

name: Takao Yasuda
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Takao Yasuda founded discount retailer Don Quijote, now Pan Pacific International Holdings, in 1980.
The retailer has nearly 750 stores and is publicly traded. It sells a wide range of products, from Rolexes to snacks to adult toys.
He returned as a board director in 2019, after having stepped down as CEO and chairman in 2015. Yasuda's title at Pan Pacific is now founding chairman and supreme advisor.
Supermarket UNY, formerly a part of retail and convenience-store operator FamilyMart UNY, is  a 100% subsidiary.
In September 2024, his 23-year-old son Yusaku was appointed to the company's board.
forbes_facts: In 2017, the company opened up its first store in Singapore, called Don Don Donki, part of an expansion in Southeast Asia.
Yasuda's first retail venture was a discount store in Tokyo called Thieves' Market, which he opened in 1978.

name: Renzo Rosso
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Renzo Rosso owns denim powerhouse Diesel plus designer brands Maison Margiela, Viktor & Rolf and Marni through his Only the Brave holding company.
Rosso got his start at age 15, when he borrowed his mother's sewing machine and made his first piece of clothing: a pair of bell-bottoms.
He later joined denim guru Adriano Goldschmied at an Italian manufacturing company called Moltex, which he renamed Diesel in 1978.
Seven years later he bought out Goldschmied's stake and positioned Diesel as an upscale choice for denim.
His family's investment vehicle, Red Circle, owns stakes in everything from mobile app companies to eyewear manufacturers.
forbes_facts: Rosso picked the name "Diesel" for his company as a nod to the oil crises after the 1973 Arab-Israeli War.
Rosso also owns Italian soccer club L.R. Vicenza Virtus and a winery named Diesel Farm.
